Propose a projected CRS for the data

Source: R/crs.R
propose_crs.Rd

Proposes the projected coordinate reference system (CRS) that keeps distances between locations closest to their values on the Earth, for computing distances and fitting geostatistical models. A WGS 84 UTM zone is proposed when it is nearly as good as the best projection, and a conformal projection centred on the data otherwise.

Usage

propose_crs(
  data,
  epsg_tolerance = 0.005,
  messages = getOption("RiskMap.messages", TRUE)
)

Arguments

data

An sf or sfc object of points or polygons, in any CRS.

epsg_tolerance

The largest distortion of distances, as a fraction, for which a UTM zone is proposed. The default of 0.005 accepts a UTM zone that distorts distances by at most 0.5% over the data.

messages

Whether to report the CRS proposed and its distortion. Defaults to the option RiskMap.messages, or TRUE if it is unset.

Value

The EPSG code of the UTM zone as an integer, or an sf crs object for a centred projection. Its name begins with "RiskMap" and gives the family, the centre (the standard parallel for the Lambert conformal conic projection), the azimuth of the oblique Mercator projection and the scale factor k0, for example "RiskMap oblique stereographic 23E 4.5S k0 0.9952". Either can be passed to sf::st_transform() and to the model_crs argument of glgpm().

Details

No planar map keeps every distance, so a projected CRS stretches or shrinks them by a factor that varies over the map. The distortion of a CRS over the data is the largest relative error of short distances over the region the data cover, measured on the WGS 84 ellipsoid (see crs_distortion()). It also bounds the relative error of every distance between two locations of the data.

The region is the convex hull of the data, whether points or polygons. Two kinds of CRS are compared.

  • The WGS 84 UTM zone at the centre of the region, the centre of the smallest spherical cap enclosing it, and its two neighbours. The hemisphere is that of the centre, with the Equator counted as north, and does not change distances.

  • Four conformal projections centred on the data: oblique stereographic, transverse Mercator, oblique Mercator and Lambert conformal conic. Their parameters minimise the largest scale error over the region (Chebyshev's criterion), and their scale factor balances the smallest and largest scale about 1. Their centres are rounded to 0.5 degrees and their scale factors to four decimals, so that data with similar extents usually get the same CRS.

Conformal projections keep angles, so a covariance that is isotropic on the Earth stays isotropic locally in the plane, and only its scale changes slightly over the map.

The best UTM zone is proposed when its distortion is at most epsg_tolerance, and the best centred projection otherwise. A region about 1,000 km across or less usually gets a UTM zone. The best centred projection keeps distances within 0.5% over every African country. No planar CRS keeps them within 1% over a region that holds a disc about 3,600 km across, such as sub-Saharan Africa, and a warning of class riskmap_warning_crs then says so.

Functions that compute distances, such as glgpm(), variogram() and create_grid(), call propose_crs() for data in longitude and latitude. When several analyses should share one CRS, for example analyses of different surveys in one country, call propose_crs() once on the country's boundary and pass the result as model_crs or distance_crs.

References

Milnor J (1969). A problem in cartography. American Mathematical Monthly 76, 1101-1112.

Snyder JP (1987). Map Projections: A Working Manual. USGS Professional Paper 1395.

See also

crs_distortion() for the distortion of any CRS over the data.

Examples

data("infect_sma")
propose_crs(infect_sma)
#> ℹ Proposed EPSG:32610 (WGS 84 / UTM zone 10N), which distorts distances by at
#>   most 0.015% over `data`.
#> [1] 32610

# A region too wide for a UTM zone gets a centred projection
library(sf)
wide <- st_as_sf(data.frame(lon = c(12, 31, 12, 31), lat = c(-13, -13, 5, 5)),
                 coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
crs <- propose_crs(wide)
#> ℹ Proposed a custom Lambert conformal conic projection, "RiskMap Lambert
#>   conformal conic 21.5E 4S k0 0.9937", which distorts distances by at most
#>   0.63% over `data`.
#> ℹ The best UTM zone, EPSG:32734 (WGS 84 / UTM zone 34S), distorts them by up to
#>   1.5%, more than `epsg_tolerance` allows.
crs$Name
#> [1] "RiskMap Lambert conformal conic 21.5E 4S k0 0.9937"
crs_distortion(wide, crs)
#>   max_error_pct max_anisotropy_pct min_scale max_scale n_locations
#> 1     0.6318523       2.107198e-06 0.9937025  1.006319        1883
